name: Real Life Trust Protocol
licence: specification text CC BY 4.0; code Apache-2.0 (trust-protocol) and MIT (app, test bench)

stack.credentials: DTG RelationshipCredential (registry context v1, issuerScope pairwise, eddsa-jcs-2022); pairwise documents under a relationship MAC
stack.transport: TSP 1.0 through the VTI mediator, routed with direct fallback; own mediator instance; the delivery port takes further carriers
stack.trustTasks: Trust Tasks framework: type URI with /spec/, JSON schema, Data Integrity proof or pairwise MAC; reads trust-task-error 0.2 to 0.6
stack.groups: a signed, replicated authority log every member holds; no owner, no admin role; policy as data; contested authority fails closed
stack.sharedState: replication contract over a key-blind carrier; key agreement behind a port (BeeKEM reference, MLS shown through the same port)
stack.devices: keys per device derived under the person, allocation of one-time keys by the person, no seed on any device (experiment E15)

trustTaskUse.note: Own types in the Trust Tasks framework; from the registry it reads trust-task-error (0.2 to 0.6) and trust-task-next-step.

vrc-exchange.note: Our encounter credential is a DTG RelationshipCredential; a conformance reader for foreign plain DTG VRCs under did:peer:2 and did:key exists with negatives. No documented run against another implementation's issuer yet.

app-change.note: Relationships are documents and travel; membership is a fact in a replicated log, not a credential a wallet carries. An outward membership statement is designed, not built.

contact-ceremony.note: encounter-scan is published in the DTGWG ceremony definition format; shared-connect is being defined jointly with Consensual on VTI trigger links, with shared binding vectors.

direct-message.note: A pairwise message document under a relationship MAC, no transferable proof. Only RLTP reads it today; we propose a shared type (scenario message-over-tsp).

membership-statement.note: Membership is invite, the subject's own signed accept, and admission under the group's stated policy, all in the log. No wallet-held VMC; an outward statement for parties outside the group is designed, not built.

multi-app-access.note: Not exercised. Would follow from the outward membership statement.

subgroups.note: A sub-group is a group with its own log and policy; no special mechanism. Not exercised across apps.

shared-room.note: Spike: a browser tab without a trust agent joins an OpenVTC Data Room, reads records and writes one that pnm reads back. Our replication contract treats a data room as a key-blind carrier. Run protocol to be published.

registry-lookup.note: A registry is a service that becomes mandatory; we have no counterpart and do not plan one. We read registry trust tasks at the adapter boundary.

did-resolution.note: did:key only, resolved locally without a network; one anchor per relationship.

offline-write.note: A write is valid when issued, never because it arrived (Access §1.3); the simulators run with no network at all.

evidence.label: Simulator: the app on three devices

ceremony-definitions.note: encounter-scan published in the DTGWG ceremony definition format; shared-connect to follow at v0.3.

same-carrier.note: TSP 1.0 through the VTI mediator, routed with direct fallback; own instance at mediator.web-of-trust.de.

cross-carrier.note: Two parties at different mediators have no TSP relationship in VTI today; the delivery port takes further carriers but none is built.

document-framework.note: Every wire artifact is a Trust Task document: type URI with /spec/, schema, Data Integrity proof or pairwise MAC. Types not yet published as a third-party source.

error-answers.note: Reads trust-task-error 0.2 to 0.6 as answers; the states each one leaves are in the envelope vector.

message-privacy.note: message@1 carries a pairwise MAC and no Data Integrity proof; only the two parties can verify it.

authority-model.note: Signed log with causal order and a rule for every concurrent pair; contested authority fails closed. Offered as a profile, not as the model others should adopt.

newcomer-history.note: History through the key chain; the retained set decides what a newcomer may open (Membership Tasks §1.3). Exercised in the test bench, not across apps.

key-agreement.note: Key world behind a port; BeeKEM reference, MLS (OpenMLS 0.9.1, 0x0001) shown through the same port in experiment E13 with the same scenarios.

captured-device.note: Test bench K4: PCS after a captured device, concurrent removals; not exercised across apps.

multi-device.note: Experiment E15: keys per device, allocation by the person, 20 scenarios; core merged, restore lifecycle open.

traditional-tools.note: A group points at its data (document.attach) and a tool asks only who belongs through the authorization view; not built.

wire-conformance.note: We use @openvtc/vti-tsp-js, the library tsp-conformance tests; a driver of our own would measure the same code.

document-conformance.note: Byte-exact vectors for every document type, re-derived by a runner; would join a shared document-level suite.

ui-consistency.note: Relationship classes met, introduced, link with colours and warnings are defined for our app; no shared vocabulary across apps yet.
